title: Reading a Handwritten Address
section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
transcript: A local history project used an artificial intelligence system to turn old postcards into searchable text. The software could usually read the printed dates, but handwritten addresses posed a different problem. To see where human review was most useful, the team drew a small sample of cards from three decades. They asked volunteers to compare the software's output with the card image before looking at its confidence score. Several faded addresses turned out to be readable, while the system was sometimes very confident about a clear address written in an unusual hand and still got it wrong. The project now checks a sample of high confidence addresses as well as difficult ones. The trial covered only one collection, however, so it cannot tell the team whether the same review policy would suit letters or diaries.

questions.prompt: What were volunteers asked to do before seeing the confidence score?
options: Find a postcard from each decade.
Compare the machine text with the card image.
Rewrite the printed dates by hand.
Rank the cards by the amount of fading.
questions.answer: Compare the machine text with the card image.
questions.explanation: 志愿者先把系统生成的文字与明信片图像对照，再查看置信度。

questions.prompt: Which unexpected error did the team notice?
options: An unusual handwriting style could lead to a confident but wrong result.
Some printed dates disappeared as volunteers edited the text.
Cards from one decade all showed the same incorrect address.
The software refused to read addresses with any visible fading.
questions.answer: An unusual handwriting style could lead to a confident but wrong result.
questions.explanation: 地址即使字迹清晰，只要书写风格少见，系统也可能在高置信度下识别错误。
